natural: share the gains equally

meaning.en: For all parties involved to share in the benefits equally.
meaning.zh: 各方都能平等地分享好处。

examples.zh: 合作的前提是风险共担、利益均沾。
examples.en: Cooperation rests on sharing the risks and sharing the gains equally.

examples.zh: 几家公司约定利益均沾，共同开发这块市场。
examples.en: The firms agreed to split the gains evenly and develop the market together.

examples.zh: 他们想搞利益均沾，谁也不肯吃亏。
examples.en: They wanted everyone to share the gains, and no one was willing to lose out.

usage.en: Predicate or attributive; neutral in tone, common in business and political writing, sometimes slightly cynical about carve-ups.
usage.zh: 多作谓语、定语，常用于商业、政治语境，有时略带讽刺。

pinyin: mó gāo yī chǐ, dào gāo yī zhàng
literal: Evil · rises · one · foot, righteousness · rises · one · zhang (ten feet)
natural: as the devil climbs a foot, the Way climbs ten

meaning.en: However much evil grows, good will outgrow it; right will win over wrong in the end.
meaning.zh: 邪恶再猖狂，正义的力量总会更强大，最终战胜邪恶。

examples.zh: 骗子手段翻新，可魔高一尺，道高一丈，警方很快就破了案。
examples.en: The fraudsters kept inventing new tricks, but the police stayed a step ahead and soon cracked the case.

examples.zh: 别担心，魔高一尺，道高一丈，邪不压正。
examples.en: Don't worry: good outgrows evil in the end, and wrong never overcomes right.

examples.zh: 网络安全就是一场魔高一尺，道高一丈的较量。
examples.en: Online security is a contest in which defenders keep out-climbing the attackers.

usage.en: A deliberate reversal of the older, pessimistic 道高一尺，魔高一丈, which says evil outgrows good; this form is the optimistic one. Used as a full saying.
usage.zh: 是对旧说“道高一尺，魔高一丈”的反用，表达乐观的态度。多作独立语句使用。

origin.source: 明·吴承恩《西游记》第五十回

story.en: Chapter 50 of Journey to the West has the line 'As the Way rises a foot, the demon rises ten feet'. The idiom reverses it to say that the Way ultimately overcomes evil, and is now used for any adversary being outdone by a stronger answer.
story.zh: 《西游记》第五十回有“道高一尺，魔高一丈”之语，指修行越深，魔障越大。后人反其意而用之，作“魔高一尺，道高一丈”，表示正义终将压倒邪恶。

natural: it is hard to be a good person

meaning.en: Being kind and fair-minded often earns you criticism or offends someone; being nice is a thankless job.
meaning.zh: 为人正直善良，往往吃力不讨好，容易得罪人或遭误解。

examples.zh: 调解邻里纠纷，两边都不讨好，真是好人难做。
examples.en: Mediating neighbours' quarrels pleases neither side; being the good guy is hard.

examples.zh: 劝了半天反被埋怨，他叹道：好人难做啊。
examples.en: After all that advice he got blamed instead, and sighed, 'Nice people have it hard.'

examples.zh: 做老师要得罪人，真是好人难做。
examples.en: A teacher has to upset people sometimes; it really is hard to be the good one.

usage.en: Independent saying, often a sigh of resignation. Often used when someone is blamed for trying to help.
usage.zh: 多作独立语句，常带无奈的感叹语气。

natural: bound feet

meaning.en: The tiny bound feet of women in imperial China, once admired as a mark of beauty; also a woman with such feet.
meaning.zh: 旧时女子缠足后形成的小脚，被视为美的标志；也指缠足的女子。

examples.zh: 奶奶那双三寸金莲，走路总是一步三摇。
examples.en: Grandmother's tiny bound feet made her sway at every step.

examples.zh: 博物馆里陈列着一双绣花的三寸金莲鞋。
examples.en: The museum displays a pair of embroidered shoes made for bound feet.

examples.zh: 缠足陋习使无数女子的三寸金莲成了终身的痛苦。
examples.en: The cruel custom of foot-binding left countless women with lifelong suffering behind their 'golden lotuses'.

usage.en: Noun. Now mainly a historical term, often with a note of criticism of foot-binding. Four standard inches here means very small.
usage.zh: 名词。现多用于历史语境，常含对缠足陋习的批评之意。

natural: an eagle soars across the sky

meaning.en: An eagle sweeping through the vast sky; a picture of freedom, vigour and boundless ambition.
meaning.zh: 雄鹰在辽阔的天空搏击飞翔，形容自由奔放、气势雄壮、志向远大。

equivalents: free as an eagle in the sky

examples.zh: 青年人要有鹰击长空的志气，不怕风雨。
examples.en: Young people should have the spirit of an eagle in the open sky and not fear the storm.

examples.zh: 海军飞行员驾机升空，鹰击长空，英姿飒爽。
examples.en: The navy pilots took off and swept across the sky, looking dashing.

examples.zh: 毕业典礼上，校长祝愿同学们鹰击长空，前程万里。
examples.en: At graduation the principal wished the students a soaring future with endless prospects.

story.en: Mao Zedong's 1925 poem looks at the autumn river and writes: 'Eagles strike the vast sky, fish glide in shallow water, ten thousand creatures vie in freedom beneath the frosty sky' (鹰击长空，鱼翔浅底，万类霜天竞自由).
story.zh: 毛泽东1925年所作《沁园春·长沙》：“鹰击长空，鱼翔浅底，万类霜天竞自由。”

usage.en: Predicate or attributive; elevated, often paired with 鱼翔浅底 ('fish glide in shallow water').
usage.zh: 多作谓语、定语，语体较书面，常与“鱼翔浅底”对举。

natural: of one voice and one spirit

meaning.en: To share the same views and outlook, so as to stand together.
meaning.zh: 志趣、观点相同，彼此呼应、一致行动。

examples.zh: 两国在这个问题上同声同气，互相支持。
examples.en: The two countries are of one voice on this issue and back each other.

examples.zh: 他们几个同声同气，常常在会上一起发言。
examples.en: The few of them think alike and often speak up together at meetings.

examples.zh: 同声同气的朋友，更容易一起做成大事。
examples.en: Like-minded friends find it easier to achieve great things together.

usage.en: Predicate; formal and slightly literary, closely related to 同声相应，同气相求.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，书面色彩较浓，与“同声相应，同气相求”意近。

natural: beat swords into ploughshares

meaning.en: To turn weapons into farm tools; to end war and turn to peaceful construction.
meaning.zh: 把兵器改铸成农具，比喻停止战争，从事和平建设。

examples.zh: 战争结束后，工厂铸剑为犁，开始生产拖拉机。
examples.en: After the war the factory beat its swords into ploughshares and began making tractors.

examples.zh: 人类的理想是铸剑为犁，永享和平。
examples.en: Humanity's dream is to beat swords into ploughshares and enjoy lasting peace.

examples.zh: 这座军工厂转产民用设备，可谓铸剑为犁。
examples.en: This arms plant switched to civilian equipment, a true case of swords into ploughshares.

usage.en: Predicate or attributive; formal. A calque of the Biblical image (Isaiah 2:4, Micah 4:3), now fully naturalised in Chinese, and close in sense to the older 化干戈为玉帛.
usage.zh: 多作谓语、定语，书面语。字面与《圣经》“将刀打成犁头”相合，现已成为通用成语，意近传统说法“化干戈为玉帛”。

pinyin: xióng jiū jiū qì áng áng
natural: valiant and high-spirited

meaning.en: Full of martial vigour and head held high; bold and spirited in bearing.
meaning.zh: 形容勇武雄壮、精神饱满、气势高昂的样子。

examples.zh: 仪仗队雄赳赳气昂昂地走过天安门广场。
examples.en: The honour guard marched across Tiananmen Square, spirited and upright.

examples.zh: 球队雄赳赳气昂昂地走进体育场。
examples.en: The team strode into the stadium full of confidence.

examples.zh: 他雄赳赳气昂昂地走上讲台，准备大干一场。
examples.en: He walked up to the podium with a spirited stride, ready to give it his all.

usage.en: Adverbial or predicate. Best known from the 1950 song 'Resist America, Aid Korea' ('Valiant, valiant, spirits high, crossing the Yalu River'); sometimes used with light humour for a swaggering gait.
usage.zh: 多作状语、谓语。因《中国人民志愿军战歌》“雄赳赳，气昂昂，跨过鸭绿江”而广为人知，有时也带诙谐意味。

natural: avoid haste, exercise patience

meaning.en: To avoid rushing and rely on restraint; a cautious, patient policy.
meaning.zh: 戒除急躁，凭借忍耐和克制行事，指稳健谨慎的方针。

examples.zh: 面对复杂局势，公司决定戒急用忍，不急于扩张。
examples.en: Facing a complicated situation, the company chose patience over haste and held off expanding.

examples.zh: 投资要戒急用忍，不能一看到行情上涨就冲进去。
examples.en: Investing calls for restraint; you can't dive in the moment the market rises.

examples.zh: 他把“戒急用忍”四个字挂在书房墙上。
examples.en: He hung the four characters 'avoid haste, use patience' on his study wall.

usage.en: Predicate or quoted maxim; formal, often in policy or business writing. Famously used in 1996 for Taiwan's cautious policy on mainland investment.
usage.zh: 多作谓语或座右铭，书面语，常见于政策、商业文章。1996年因台湾对大陆投资的政策而为人熟知。

natural: work out petty calculations

meaning.en: To calculate for one's own petty gain; to be narrowly self-interested.
meaning.zh: 只为自己的一点小利盘算，形容斤斤计较、自私。

equivalents: have an eye on one's own petty gains

examples.zh: 团队合作时，大家都打小算盘，项目就做不成。
examples.en: If everyone in a team plays the small-calculation game, the project cannot succeed.

examples.zh: 他处处打小算盘，同事们都不愿跟他共事。
examples.en: He is calculating over every little thing, and colleagues do not want to work with him.

examples.zh: 别光顾着打小算盘，要顾全大局。
examples.en: Don't think only about your own petty interests; keep the big picture in mind.

usage.en: Verb phrase, usually split: 打自己的小算盘. Colloquial and mildly critical.
usage.zh: 动宾短语，常拆开用，如“打自己的小算盘”。口语，略含贬义。

natural: having only the name

meaning.en: To exist in name only, without the substance to match.
meaning.zh: 只有名义、名声，而没有相应的实际内容。

examples.zh: 这所大学徒有其名，师资和设备都很差。
examples.en: The university has a name but little else; its staff and facilities are poor.

examples.zh: 这座“名胜古迹”徒有其名，其实根本没什么可看。
examples.en: This 'famous site' is famous in name only; there is really nothing to see.

examples.zh: 他的头衔不少，却徒有其名，没有实权。
examples.en: He holds many titles, but only in name, with no real power.

usage.en: Predicate. Close to 徒有虚名 and 名不副实; the phrase is a little more neutral in tone.
usage.zh: 多作谓语。与“徒有虚名”“名不副实”意近，语气稍平和。

text: 任凭风浪起，稳坐钓鱼船
pinyin: rèn píng fēng làng qǐ, wěn zuò diào yú chuán
literal: no matter · wind and waves · rise, steadily · sit · fishing · boat
natural: let the waves rise, I sit steady in my fishing boat

meaning.en: However rough things get, stay calm and unmoved.
meaning.zh: 不管风浪多大，都镇定自若、稳如泰山。

examples.zh: 股市大跌，他却说任凭风浪起，稳坐钓鱼船。
examples.en: The stock market plunged, yet he said he would sit tight whatever storm came.

examples.zh: 遇事要有定力，任凭风浪起，稳坐钓鱼船。
examples.en: Face things with composure; however high the waves, stay steady in your boat.

examples.zh: 公司内部动荡，只有老张任凭风浪起，稳坐钓鱼船。
examples.en: With the company in turmoil, only Lao Zhang stayed unmoved as the waves rose.

usage.en: Independent saying, often said of someone who stays calm in a crisis, or sometimes of someone who refuses to act. Often also heard as 稳坐钓鱼台.
usage.zh: 多作独立语句，形容在危机中镇定自若，有时也指按兵不动。也常说成“稳坐钓鱼台”。

literal: so as to · observe · later · effect
natural: to watch how things turn out

meaning.en: To hold off from further action and see what the person's later conduct shows, often after a warning or a reduced penalty.
meaning.zh: 暂缓处理，等待观察以后的表现或效果，多用于对过失者的处分。

equivalents: to see how things go from here

examples.zh: 对他免于处分，以观后效。
examples.en: He was let off punishment, to see how he behaves from here.

examples.zh: 先暂缓执行，以观后效。
examples.en: Hold off on carrying it out for now and see what happens.

examples.zh: 法院判处缓刑，以观后效。
examples.en: The court gave a suspended sentence, to observe his later conduct.

usage.en: Set phrase at the end of a clause; legal and administrative register.
usage.zh: 多用于句末，法律、行政语体。

natural: three kneelings and nine kowtows

meaning.en: The most solemn court ritual of the Qing, three kneelings with three head-knockings each; also grovelling submission.
meaning.zh: 清代朝见皇帝的最隆重的礼节：行三次跪拜，每次叩头三下，共九叩；也比喻卑躬屈膝。

examples.zh: 使臣在殿前行三跪九叩之礼。
examples.en: The envoy performed the three kneelings and nine kowtows before the hall.

examples.zh: 他对上司三跪九叩，只想求个好差事。
examples.en: He grovelled before his boss, just to get a good post.

examples.zh: 英国使团拒绝行三跪九叩的礼节，引起争议。
examples.en: The British mission's refusal to perform the three kneelings and nine kowtows caused a dispute.

usage.en: Noun; used literally of the ritual or figuratively of excessive deference.
usage.zh: 名词，既指礼仪，也比喻过分的恭顺。

natural: watery clear soup

meaning.en: Thin, bland food with little oil or flavour; also dull, uninteresting writing or life.
meaning.zh: 汤水清淡、没有油水，形容饭菜寡淡；也比喻内容平淡无味。

examples.zh: 食堂的菜清汤寡水，一点油星都没有。
examples.en: The canteen food is thin and watery without a trace of oil.

examples.zh: 这篇文章写得清汤寡水，读来索然无味。
examples.en: The article is bland and watery, dull to read.

examples.zh: 天天清汤寡水的日子，他真过够了。
examples.en: He has had enough of days of thin soup and nothing else.

usage.en: Adjectival or predicate; colloquial, mildly critical.
usage.zh: 多作谓语、定语，口语，略含贬义。

natural: in safety, do not forget danger

meaning.en: To stay alert to possible danger even in peaceful, secure times.
meaning.zh: 处在安定的环境里，不忘记可能出现的危险。

equivalents: never drop your guard in peacetime

examples.zh: 国家要做到安不忘危，才能长治久安。
examples.en: A country must stay alert in peacetime if it is to remain secure for long.

examples.zh: 企业越是顺利，越要安不忘危。
examples.en: The smoother things go for a firm, the more it must remember risk.

examples.zh: 消防演练就是为了让大家安不忘危。
examples.en: Fire drills are there so that everyone stays mindful of danger.

story.en: The Appendix says that the gentleman 'in safety does not forget danger, in survival does not forget ruin, in order does not forget chaos' (君子安而不忘危，存而不忘亡，治而不忘乱).
story.zh: 《周易·系辞下》：“君子安而不忘危，存而不忘亡，治而不忘乱，是以身安而国家可保也。”

usage.en: Predicate; formal. Often paired with 存不忘亡，治不忘乱, and nearly the same as 居安思危.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，书面语。常与“存不忘亡，治不忘乱”并用，与“居安思危”意近。

literal: all under heaven · return to · heart
natural: the whole world turns its heart to him

meaning.en: For the people everywhere to give their loyalty and support to a ruler.
meaning.zh: 天下的人心都归向、拥护某一人或某一方。

examples.zh: 只有施行仁政，才能使天下归心。
examples.en: Only a humane government can win the hearts of all.

examples.zh: 他广纳贤才，终于天下归心。
examples.en: He welcomed talent far and wide and finally won everyone's loyalty.

examples.zh: 在乱世中，天下归心的人往往能成就大业。
examples.en: In troubled times, whoever wins the hearts of the realm can achieve great things.

usage.en: Predicate; formal and slightly literary.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，书面语，略带文言色彩。

pinyin: wáng gù zuǒ yòu ér yán tā
literal: the king · glance at · left · right · and · speak of · other things
natural: the king looked to left and right and talked of something else

meaning.en: To dodge an awkward question by changing the subject.
meaning.zh: 回头看着左右的人，说别的事，比喻回避问题，转移话题。

examples.zh: 记者追问细节，发言人却王顾左右而言他。
examples.en: When reporters pressed for details, the spokesman simply changed the subject.

examples.zh: 一提到还钱，他就王顾左右而言他。
examples.en: The moment repayment came up, he turned to talk of other things.

examples.zh: 面对尴尬的提问，他只好王顾左右而言他。
examples.en: Faced with an awkward question, he had to talk of something else.

story.en: Mencius asks King Xuan of Qi what to do with a man who entrusts his family to a friend and finds them starving, and then what to do with an official who cannot govern. The king agrees each time, but when asked about his own failures, he 'looked left and right and spoke of something else'.
story.zh: 《孟子·梁惠王下》：孟子问齐宣王，士师不能管好下属怎么办，王说“已之”；再问“四境之内不治，则如之何”，“王顾左右而言他”。

usage.en: Predicate; often used to criticise evasiveness, and sometimes shortened to 顾左右而言他.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，批评回避问题的态度，也可缩略为“顾左右而言他”。

natural: a single pillar holds up the sky

meaning.en: A single towering pillar propping up the heavens; a person or force that bears the whole burden.
meaning.zh: 一根柱子撑住天，形容人或事物坚强有力，起着中流砥柱的作用，也形容高耸直立。

equivalents: a pillar holding up the sky

examples.zh: 全公司的重担，几乎靠他一柱擎天。
examples.en: The whole company's burden rested almost on his shoulders alone.

examples.zh: 这根石柱高耸入云，宛如一柱擎天。
examples.en: The stone column soars into the clouds like a pillar holding up the sky.

examples.zh: 危难之际，她一柱擎天，撑起了这个家。
examples.en: In the crisis she bore the load alone and held the family together.

usage.en: Predicate or adverbial; literary, used of a person or a tall structure.
usage.zh: 多作谓语、状语，书面语，可指人，也可指高耸的建筑。

natural: first try of the voice

meaning.en: To make a first public attempt, especially a striking one, such as a debut.
meaning.zh: 原指初次发出啼叫，比喻初次登台或初次做事就表现不凡。

examples.zh: 新人导演初试啼声，作品就获了大奖。
examples.en: The new director made a debut and won a major prize with the first film.

examples.zh: 这位歌手在晚会上初试啼声，博得满堂彩。
examples.en: The singer made her debut at the gala to great applause.

examples.zh: 他在国际比赛初试啼声，就拿到金牌。
examples.en: He tried his first international contest and took gold straight away.

usage.en: Predicate; used for a first appearance that goes well. Not for a failed first attempt.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，指首次尝试且表现出色。

natural: short of food and clothing

meaning.en: To lack the basics of food and clothing; to live in poverty.
meaning.zh: 吃的、穿的都不够，形容生活贫困。

equivalents: not have enough to eat or wear

examples.zh: 那些年家里缺吃少穿，孩子们常常饿着肚子。
examples.en: Back then the family had too little to eat or wear, and the children often went hungry.

examples.zh: 他从小缺吃少穿，所以特别珍惜现在的生活。
examples.en: He grew up in want of food and clothes, so he cherishes his life today.

examples.zh: 灾区的老乡缺吃少穿，急需援助。
examples.en: People in the disaster zone lack food and clothing and urgently need aid.

usage.en: Predicate; a colloquial counterpart of the more formal 缺衣少食.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，是较书面的“缺衣少食”的口语说法。

natural: the year of the smooth ear

meaning.en: The age of sixty, when Confucius said he could hear things without friction.
meaning.zh: 指六十岁。孔子说六十岁时“耳顺”，对听到的话能明辨是非，不觉逆耳。

examples.zh: 老教授年逾耳顺之年，仍坚持在一线教学。
examples.en: The old professor, past sixty, still teaches on the front line.

examples.zh: 他到了耳顺之年，性情越发平和。
examples.en: By his sixtieth year he had grown ever more mild.

examples.zh: 父亲耳顺之年，我们全家为他办了寿宴。
examples.en: For Father's sixtieth birthday the whole family held a banquet.

story.en: Confucius summed up his life: 'At fifteen I set my heart on learning... at sixty my ear was attuned' (六十而耳顺).
story.zh: 《论语·为政》：“吾十有五而志于学，三十而立，四十而不惑，五十而知天命，六十而耳顺，七十而从心所欲，不逾矩。”

date.zh: 春秋末至战国初 · 前5—前4世纪
date.en: late Spring and Autumn to early Warring States, 5th–4th c. BC

usage.en: Noun; polite and literary term for the age of sixty, like 花甲之年 (which stresses the sixty-year cycle). The other Confucian ages are 而立, 不惑, 知命.
usage.zh: 名词，是对六十岁的雅称。与“花甲之年”相近；孔子所说的其他年龄有“而立”“不惑”“知命”。

natural: lord over a region alone

meaning.en: To dominate a region single-handedly, usually by force.
meaning.zh: 独自称霸一个地区，多含贬义。

examples.zh: 这个黑帮在城东独霸一方，无人敢惹。
examples.en: The gang ruled the east of the city, and no one dared cross it.

examples.zh: 他靠着背景独霸一方，当地人敢怒不敢言。
examples.en: He lorded it over the area with his connections while locals dared not speak.

examples.zh: 这家企业在行业里独霸一方，不让别人分一杯羹。
examples.en: The firm dominates its sector and lets no one else take a share.

usage.en: Predicate; usually critical, of a bully, gang or monopoly.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，多含贬义，常指恶势力或垄断者。

natural: gloomily unable to achieve one's aims

meaning.en: To feel depressed because one cannot fulfil one's ambitions.
meaning.zh: 因抱负不能实现而心情压抑苦闷。

equivalents: stew in frustration at one's lack of success

examples.zh: 他一生郁郁不得志，直到晚年才得到认可。
examples.en: He lived his life gloomy and unfulfilled and was only recognised in old age.

examples.zh: 这位诗人怀才不遇，郁郁不得志而终。
examples.en: The poet was never given his chance and died disappointed.

examples.zh: 别因一时失意就郁郁不得志，机会还多着呢。
examples.en: Don't brood on a passing setback; there will be more chances.

usage.en: Predicate or adverbial; literary. 得志 'achieve one's goals' is a verb-object compound.
usage.zh: 多作谓语、状语，书面语。“得志”是动宾结构，指实现志向。

natural: mountains and rivers outside and in

meaning.en: A country or region whose mountains and rivers form natural defences, inside and out.
meaning.zh: 外有大河，内有高山，指地势险要、形势有利。

equivalents: a natural fortress of hills and rivers
a land well guarded by nature

examples.zh: 山西表里山河，自古是兵家必争之地。
examples.en: Shanxi, ringed by mountains and the Yellow River, has long been a prize for armies.

examples.zh: 这座古城表里山河，易守难攻。
examples.en: With mountains and rivers on every side, the ancient city is easy to defend and hard to attack.

examples.zh: 他向君主进言，称此地表里山河，足以立国。
examples.en: He told the ruler that the land was guarded by mountains and rivers and could found a state.

story.en: Before the battle of Chengpu, Duke Wen of Jin's adviser said that, if Jin won, its land 'with the Yellow River outside and mountains within' (表里山河) would suffer no harm.
story.zh: 《左传·僖公二十八年》：城濮之战前，子犯劝晋文公：“战而捷，必得诸侯；若其不捷，表里山河，必无害也。”

usage.en: Attributive or predicate; literary, often of Shanxi (山西) in the description of the Jin state.
usage.zh: 多作定语、谓语，书面语，常用来形容晋地山西。

natural: to view it thus

meaning.en: To look at things in a certain way; to hold such a view.
meaning.zh: 用这样的态度、观点来看待事物。

examples.zh: 对于这次失败，我们应作如是观：它是一次学习的机会。
examples.en: We should view this failure so: as a chance to learn.

examples.zh: 世事无常，作如是观，心里便平静许多。
examples.en: Things change; looking at it so brings a good deal of calm.

examples.zh: 他对金钱作如是观，所以活得很自在。
examples.en: He sees money in this way, and so lives at ease.

story.en: The Diamond Sutra closes: 'All conditioned things are like a dream, an illusion, a bubble, a shadow... one should view them thus' (应作如是观).
story.zh: 《金刚经》：“一切有为法，如梦幻泡影，如露亦如电，应作如是观。”

usage.en: Predicate; formal, often preceded by a description of the way of seeing ('对…作如是观').
usage.zh: 多作谓语，书面语，常说“对……作如是观”。

natural: straightforward and neat

meaning.en: Direct and efficient, with no hesitation or loose ends.
meaning.zh: 说话、做事爽快利索，不拖泥带水。

examples.zh: 她办事干脆利落，从不拖拉。
examples.en: She works crisply and efficiently and never drags her feet.

examples.zh: 他干脆利落地回答了所有问题。
examples.en: He answered every question briskly and directly.

examples.zh: 这一脚射门干脆利落，直挂球网死角。
examples.en: It was a clean, sharp shot straight into the top corner.

usage.en: Predicate, complement or adverbial; neutral, used of speech, actions and style. 落 is read luo in 利落.
usage.zh: 可作谓语、补语、状语；用于言行风格。“利落”的“落”读轻声。

pinyin: yī kuài shí tou luò le dì
natural: a stone has dropped to the ground

meaning.en: To feel a great relief once a long-standing worry is settled.
meaning.zh: 压在心头的担忧终于解除，感到放心、轻松。

examples.zh: 听到手术成功的消息，全家人一块石头落了地。
examples.en: On hearing the operation had succeeded, the whole family felt a weight lift.

examples.zh: 考完最后一门，我心里一块石头落了地。
examples.en: After the last exam, a stone dropped from my heart.

examples.zh: 货终于平安到港，老板一块石头落地，笑了起来。
examples.en: With the cargo safely in port, the boss felt the stone drop and began to smile.

usage.en: Predicate or clause; colloquial. Often described as 心里一块石头落了地.
usage.zh: 多作谓语或分句，口语，常说“心里一块石头落了地”。
